memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'He shall take out the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar as a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD. The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the food offerings presented to the LORD.'" - Lev 2:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
For the second time in this short chapter, we read the same two facts: a memorial portion rises to God, and the rest sustains His servants. God repeats it because it matters.

Here is a pattern worth carrying into your own life. What is given to God is never wasted, and it rarely stops with God alone. Some of it ascends in pure worship. Much of it comes back down to feed people.

Think of how this works in practice. The money you give quietly to your church becomes a pastor's rent, a widow's groceries, a child's education. The hour you spend praying for someone becomes their strength on a hard day. The gift you offer God has a way of landing in somebody's kitchen.

Jesus taught this economy plainly: give, and it will be given to you (Lk 6:38) — not as a formula for getting rich, but as a description of how God's generosity circulates. And the writer of Hebrews joins the two halves together: do not forget to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased (Heb 13:16).

Vertical worship and horizontal generosity are not rivals. In Leviticus they came from the same basket of flour.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I separate "worshipping God" from "caring for people," when Scripture holds them together?
2. Is there something I could give this week that would both honour God and feed someone?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, let what I offer You rise to Your glory and land in someone's need. Make my worship and my generosity one thing. Amen.
